subject: scale parameters : half-cauchy vs uniform giving widely different results

messages.author: a997b66afa263bd1
messages.subject: scale parameters : half-cauchy vs uniform giving widely different results
parts:
Hi Stan-users

I know discussion of scale parameters have been discussed heavily in the forums, but I still couldn't find what I was looking for. I have a simple hierarchial regression model where I define the priors like:
sigma_a ~cauchy(0,2.5);
a~ normal(0, sigma_a);

and

sigma_y ~cauchy(0,2.5);
y~ normal(0, sigma_y);

This sometimes causes "negetive scale parameters" warnings to be thrown up when stan is run. So I thought I can replace them with uniform(0,5) priors to restrict the negative scale parameters. However this gives wildly off-the chart parameter estimates and the 'dependent variable' estimate generated via the generated quantites block is nothing close to expected.  I read Andrew Gelman's paper on scale parameter ( http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/published/taumain.pdf ) and I don't understand why this should happen. Any clues?
Thanks

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] scale parameters : half-cauchy vs uniform giving widely different results
parts:
Could you send us the whole model? If you have declared a parameter
with a lower=0 constraint, it should not be possible for it to be negative.
If you think you have an example, please send it to us with data to try
to recreate the problem.

If you try to use uniform(0,5), you need an upper=5 constraint, too.
But we don't recommend hard constraints like this.

- Bob
